subject: Battlecard No. 023 — Windmill (partial, Helm-authorized, L2 Watch)
summary:
Published a partial battlecard for Windmill — Inspired Capital-backed $12M seed (28 April 2026) building a 'context graph' for workforce evidence over Slack, GitHub, Google Workspace, and 30+ tools. Authorized by Helm on 2026-06-04 with a specific three-section scope: (1) verified-vs-claimed architecture, (2) the four-layer model (People / Evidence / Expectations / Perspectives) evaluated against the Stratum substrate threshold, (3) two named falsifiable escalation milestones. Level 2 Watch. No defensive content from Compass; no customer outreach; no board notification — Windmill does not clear that bar.

The Windmill case is asymmetric: substrate-threat probability in a 6–12 month window reads at ~12–15% (architecture and team shape do not point this way — the public material describes an evidence-aggregation surface for performance reviews with an LLM chat layer on top, branded 'context graph'; cross-system identity resolution, time-as-edge, and per-edge consent are all absent from public description). Positioning-threat probability reads materially higher at ~45–55% — 'context graph' / 'workforce graph' travels well in trade press as a category noun and Inspired's portfolio companies typically get a second press wave 4–8 weeks after announcement (mid-July deadline for Stratum's methodology to be the canonical citation). Helm tightened the original 60-day monitoring window to 30 days on the second-press-wave reasoning. Eglin concurs with the tightening.

Founder background note worth recording: both Max Shaw (CEO) and Brian Distelburger (co-founder) come from Yext, where they built a knowledge graph for public business data. The schema-and-entity-resolution chops are real; whether that DNA scales into the consent-bound, time-aware workforce shape an HR substrate requires is the open question the public material does not engage with.

Two escalation triggers, both public-signal (no private intelligence required):
  (A) Series A announcement using substrate vocabulary — 'system of record,' 'graph database,' 'identity resolution across systems,' or claims of architectural depth exceeding evidence-surface framing. Watcher: Eglin. Cadence: weekly funding-news sweep. Notify Helm + Compass within 24h. Action: full battlecard within 7 days.
  (B) Named reference customer using graph vocabulary in a published case study (not Windmill's own marketing copy) — Kalshi, Rho, Merge, or any future named customer describing what Windmill does for them as a 'graph,' 'substrate,' 'system of record,' or 'single source of truth.' Watcher: Eglin. Cadence: monthly customer-content sweep + Tier-A analyst publications. Same notification + action.

If 90 days pass with no triggers fired and no Series A signal, Eglin reassesses and either downgrades from L2 Watch or maintains with revised expected-trigger dates.

The synthesis from §2 (for record): for Windmill to threaten Stratum's substrate claim, they would have to ship (X) hard cross-system identity resolution with a published reconciliation algorithm and audit trail, (Y) a persistent time-versioned graph store with consent metadata on every edge and per-evidence-class deletion APIs, and (Z) an explicit governance posture (third-party bias audit, named LLM provider, model cards) once their inferences begin to influence employment outcomes. The team shape they raised on does not suggest they intend to.

Follow-up handoffs:
  • Helm — owns the strategic call if either trigger fires; partial-battlecard format authorized for proportional response patterns going forward.
  • Compass — no defensive content authorized; if Trigger B fires (customer adopts graph vocabulary), Compass updates the buyer-facing competitive page with a Windmill row in the vocabulary map (parallel to the Cornerstone row).
  • Forge — no immediate action; if Trigger A fires with 'graph database' or 'identity resolution' specifics, Forge reviews any published Windmill architecture material for technical-claims verification.
  • Kernel — no immediate action; if Windmill names an LLM provider or publishes a model card, Kernel reviews for AI-trust posture comparison.
